conclusions: Local frozen and ARM default comparisons preserve identical 8-column trajectories and identical ATE.
ARM default candidate reduces CPU/P95 slightly but does not solve difficult accuracy or the 8.2 s gap.
pin67 + threads1 + schur_ekf is a repeatable performance opt-in: easy CPU ~31-32% lower and P95 ~50-52% lower, with ATE unchanged.
pin67 + threads1 medium improves CPU/P95 (~-32.1%/-50.2%) with unchanged ATE; repeated data remains single-run except easy.
difficult Schur remains unreliable: ATE ~19.5772 m, 8.2 s gap, and 3 restart requests/reset entries.

Ceres difficult full-coverage ATE is 11.3486 m (1103 poses); on the common 994 timestamps, Schur is 19.6152 m and Ceres is 10.5793 m, so full-coverage ATE is not directly rankable. Ceres still fails the extra <1 m screening criterion (not user acceptance); no easy/medium follow-up and no Ceres default recommendation.
No all-scenario optimal satisfying difficult accuracy was found. Product defaults and calibration remain unchanged; initialization/Schur root cause remains unresolved.
ARM microbench 3-round alternation shows ~5% lower reduce/update (small sample); local x86 update has no stable improvement. Allocation probe supports fewer calls/bytes, not lower RSS.
